title: C1606 — Ignition coil-on-plug 6 connector
introduction:
The coil-on-plug unit makes the high voltage for its spark plug; this sheet helps you understand the connections serving that unit. I use the connector identity and housing drawing together, then follow each cavity into its complete table row. Keep the engine qualifier beside the control-circuit description: matching wire labels do not make the engine-specific entries interchangeable. Think of the connector shape as the envelope and the circuit description as the address—both deserve a look.

This is a connector-reading guide. It does not teach physical access, unplugging, probing, replacement-wire selection or pigtail installation. The viewing direction and the conventions behind Gauge, Size and Used are not defined here. Unqualified supply rows therefore remain reference entries rather than instructions for choosing a wire. The summary Pin Count disagrees with the drawing and pigtail cavity listing; that discrepancy remains unresolved.

edits.why: I navigate this drawing by its rounded housing, left-side projections and vertically arranged cavities. The outlined upper and lower circles flank a shaded center, which corresponds to the assignment row without a circuit or function. Those visible housing features help compare the drawing with the identity record; they do not establish release movements, locking functions or which physical side you should view.

Read the control connection across the entire row, preserving the relationship between engine qualifier, coil designation and terminal entry. Repeated rows are not extra cavities. The lower cavity carries the supply described as a fuse-or-circuit-breaker connection, and its alternate Gauge entries have no stated applicability rule. This explains the circuit roles without choosing a protective device, replacement wire or test point. Any diagnostic work needs the matching engine procedure.

The pigtail provides a connector with wire leads. I read Service Part as the service-assembly reference and Engineering Shell as the housing reference, keeping their identities distinct. Its separate Gauge entry is not permission to substitute wire for the vehicle’s circuit. The listing supports identification; deciding on replacement and carrying out a splice require the relevant repair instructions.

originalAuthorHold: The metadata Pin Count conflicts with the cavity count shown in the illustration and the pigtail Cavities entry. The discrepancy requires review; the original data remains unchanged.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 33 primary units, both complete source pages and sole figure, and 3 edits. Pin Count and unqualified supply-gauge applicability ambiguity retained for bounded identification reading only.
